tooley.q: In an optical fibre, the refractive index of the core is:
tooley.explain: n₁ > n₂ is required for total internal reflection at the core-cladding boundary.

tooley.q: A suitable optical transmitter for use with an optical fibre is:
tooley.explain: The transmitter is an infrared LED or a low-power laser diode; the photodiode and phototransistor are receivers (Tooley 10.3).

tooley.q: The typical core diameter for a monomode fibre is:
tooley.explain: Figure 10.5: single-mode core 5 µm, cladding 125 µm; multimode 50 µm.

tooley.q: In a multicore fibre-optic cable:
tooley.explain: Tooley 10.4.1: the buffers are colour coded blue, red, green, yellow and white to identify the fibres.

tooley.q: The typical wavelength of light in a fibre is:
tooley.explain: Near-infrared 1.3 µm (1310 nm), together with 0.85 and 1.55 µm.

tooley.q: What aircraft standard applies to fibre-optic networks?
tooley.explain: ARINC 636, adapted from FDDI, for the Boeing 777 AVLAN and CABLAN (up to 100 Mbps).

tooley.q: If a launcher has an acceptance angle of 45°, the corresponding numerical aperture will be:
tooley.explain: NA = sin θa = sin 45° = 0.707.

tooley.q: The typical cladding diameter for a monomode fibre is:
tooley.explain: The cladding is 125 µm (Figure 10.5).

tooley.q: If the numerical aperture of a fibre has a value of 1, this indicates that:
opts: all of the light from the source is captured by the fibre
none of the light from the source is captured by the fibre
50 per cent of the light from the source is captured by the fibre
tooley.explain: NA = 1 means θa = 90°: every ray from the source is captured (ideal).

tooley.q: When replacing a length of multi-way fibre-optic cable, it is essential to ensure that:
opts: none of the red band is covered when the coupling nut is tightened
all of the red band is covered when the coupling nut is tightened
the connectors are correctly aligned prior to mating the plug and the receptacle
tooley.explain: Align before mating. A correct connection has the red band at least 50% covered (not 0% or 100%).

tooley.q: In order to support a high data rate, a fibre-optic cable should have:
tooley.explain: Maximum data rate goes with bandwidth (Tooley 10.3).

tooley.q: A significant advantage of fibre-optic networks in large passenger aircraft is:
tooley.explain: Reduced weight, saving up to about 1,300 kg.

tooley.q: A beam of light is incident at the critical angle at a boundary between two media of different refractive index. The emerging ray will travel:
tooley.explain: At θc, θr = 90°: the refracted ray runs along the boundary.

tooley.q: The bandwidth of an optical fibre is limited by:
opts: attenuation and cross-talk in the cable
the number and severity of bends in the cable
modal dispersion occurring in the cable
tooley.explain: Dispersion stretches pulses and sets the maximum bit rate (Tooley 10.3).

tooley.q: Light propagates in a fibre optic by means of:
tooley.explain: A chain of total internal reflections at the core-cladding boundary.

tooley.q: The attenuation of an optical fibre is typically:
opts: between 2 dB and 20 dB per km
tooley.explain: Tooley 10.2.2: good-quality fibre is below 2 dB/km at 1.3 µm (the lecture gives 0.2 to 0.5 dB/km at 1550 nm).

tooley.q: The main advantage of monomode fibres is:
tooley.explain: No modal dispersion, so the highest bandwidth; in exchange for cost and harder splicing.

tooley.q: A pulse of infrared light travelling down a multimode fibre optic becomes stretched. This is due to:
tooley.explain: Modes travel different path lengths and so arrive at different times.

tooley.q: Attenuation in an optical fibre is due to:
tooley.explain: Absorption, scattering (in the core and at the boundary) and radiation at bends (Tooley 10.2.2). Dispersion is a different effect.

tooley.q: Light waves in fibre-optic cables are:
tooley.explain: 850, 1310, 1550 nm are all near-infrared, so not visible.

floyd.q: Which data transmission media does Floyd list?
opts: Wire, coaxial cable, twisted pair cable, optical fiber cable, and wireless
Only wire, coaxial cable and shielded twisted pair cable
Only optical fiber cable, radio waves and satellite links
floyd.src: Floyd Ch.13 · Section 13-1 Checkup #1 (p.745; answer p.797)

floyd.q: According to Floyd, what kind of fibre is 8.3/125 µm?
opts: Multimode, 8.3 µm core and 125 µm cladding
Single-mode, 8.3 µm core and 125 µm cladding
Multimode, 125 µm core and 8.3 µm cladding
floyd.explain: Floyd: 50/125 and 62.5/125 are multimode; 8.3/125 is single-mode (first number core, second cladding).

floyd.q: What is the main disadvantage of fibre-optic data transmission according to Floyd?
opts: Susceptibility to EMI in the aircraft environment
Cost, higher than coax, UTP and STP
Lower data rate than ordinary coaxial cable
floyd.explain: Floyd p.742: fibre is not susceptible to EMI and is faster; the main disadvantage is cost.

floyd.q: Which Floyd connector is duplex, holding two fibres for two-way communication?
floyd.explain: Floyd: ST is common for multimode, MT is a 12-fibre ribbon connector, FDDI is duplex.

floyd.q: Which description of single mode in an optical fibre matches Floyd's answer?
opts: Light travels as a single ray, the core is smaller than multimode, more bandwidth and distance but costlier
Light does not reflect but travels straight through the cladding, so no high-index core is needed
Light travels in many rays through a large core, with lower bandwidth and a lower price than multimode
